newsitem.title: USA: Fed move may lead to US corp bond spread widening.
newsitem.headline: Fed move may lead to US corp bond spread widening.

text.p: A Federal Reserve monetary tightening aimed at tempering U.S. economic growth could mark the beginning of the end for historically tight corporate bond spreads, market players said.

"If this is the first move designed to slow down the economy, this will start to put doubt into people's minds about corporate bonds," said Peter Hegel, chief investment officer for fixed income at Van Kampen American Capital.
"This probably gets the process of widening-spreads going," said Hegel, who oversees $26 billion in assets.

Hegel said spreads in the overall corporate bond market could widen gradually by 10 to 20 basis points over the rest of the year, assuming the Fed continues to tighten interest rates at least one more time as he expects.
He said the spread widening is likely to be more severe among lower-credit-quality bonds and credits issued by companies in cyclical industries such as steel, autos, paper, and chemicals.
